newsitem.title: USA: U.S. biker gang members hit with indictments.
newsitem.headline: U.S. biker gang members hit with indictments.

text.p: Federal officials on Tuesday announced the indictment of 17 motorcyle gang members from three states who they said were responsible for six murders, a war on rival gangs, bombings, theft and drug-trafficking.
The Outlaws Motorcycle Club members from Wisconsin, Illinois and Indiana were charged with 34 criminal acts under the federal racketeering law.
"The indictment charges that the Outlaws are more than a motorcycle club," said Tom Schneider, U.S. attorney for eastern Wisconsin.
"They are a sophisticated and dangerous organised crime group which has repeatedly resorted to bombinmgs and murder to protect their ongoing criminal enterprise," he said.
"Today is the beginning of the end of their trail of murders, bombings, drugs and stolen vehicles," Schneider said.

The six slayings mentioned in the indictments occurred as part of a turf war between the Outlaws and the Hells's Angels and other related clubs, and happened between 1992 and 1995 in Wisconsin, Illinois and New York.
The bombings included attempts on lives and the destruction of Hell's Angels and Hell's Henchmen clubhouses from 1990 to 1994 in Illinois, Wisconsin and Minnesota.
The "pattern of racketeering" detailed in the indictments also alleged the men shipped stolen Harley-Davidson motorcycles from the United States to Germany, peddled drugs and used counterfeit money.
Among those indicted wsere the presidents of Outlaws chapters in LaCrosse, Wisconsin, on Chicago's South Side and in Gary, Indiana, as well as the Chicago regional president of the group.
